meta.titre: Output Devices: softcopy, hardcopy, screens and printers compared
meta.sous_theme: Softcopy and hardcopy, monitors, printers and resolution

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A secretary at a secondary school in Bamenda types the Form 5 timetable on a computer. She first checks it on the screen, then prints copies to pin on the notice board. The screen version is temporary and the paper version is permanent, yet both are produced by output devices. In the GCE you are asked to name these devices, to tell softcopy from hardcopy and to compare printers. Good answers use the exact technical words.

items: Input devices such as the keyboard and the mouse send data into the computer.
The CPU processes data and then sends the result to an output device.
A picture on a screen is made of very small dots called pixels.

sections.titre: Output devices: softcopy, hardcopy, screens and printers
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What an output device is

An **output device** is a piece of hardware that receives processed data from the computer and presents it to the user as information that people can see, hear or hold. Output comes in two forms.

| Form | Meaning | Typical devices | Main features |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Softcopy** | Output shown on a screen or played through a speaker, with no physical form | Monitor, projector, speakers | Temporary, disappears when the display changes or the power goes off; easy to edit; uses no paper |
| **Hardcopy** | Output printed on paper or another physical material | Printer, plotter | Permanent; can be carried and read without a computer; uses paper and ink or toner |

### Common output devices

- **Monitor**: shows text, pictures and video. A **CRT** (Cathode Ray Tube) monitor is deep, heavy and uses more power. An **LCD** (Liquid Crystal Display) monitor is flat, light and saves desk space and electricity. Screen size is measured diagonally in inches.
- **Projector**: enlarges the screen image onto a wall or a white screen so that a whole class can see it.
- **Speakers and headphones**: produce sound output.
- **Printer**: produces hardcopy (see below).
- **Plotter**: draws large, accurate plans and maps with pens or ink, used by architects and engineers.

### Types of printer

- **Dot matrix (impact) printer**: a head of tiny pins strikes an inked ribbon against the paper. It is noisy and its print quality is low, but it can print through several layers of paper at once, so it is used for multi-part forms.
- **Inkjet printer**: sprays tiny drops of liquid ink. It gives good colour pictures and is cheap to buy, but replacing the ink can be costly.
- **Laser printer**: uses toner powder fixed to the page by heat. It is fast, quiet and sharp, which suits large numbers of pages.

### Resolution

The **sharpness** of a screen image is its **resolution**: the number of pixels across multiplied by the number of pixels down, for example 800 by 600. More pixels means a sharper picture. Total pixels = columns $\times$ rows. Printer sharpness is measured in **dots per inch (dpi)**.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question describes a job and asks which printer fits
variantes.contenu_markdown: Match the job to the feature. Many pages, quickly and sharply: laser. Coloured photos for a small print run: inkjet. Several copies of one form in a single pass: dot matrix, because the pins strike through the layers. Always give the feature that justifies the choice, not just the name.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question compares CRT and LCD monitors or asks about sharpness
variantes.contenu_markdown: A CRT monitor is bulky, heavy and uses more power. An LCD monitor is slim and light and uses less power. Sharpness depends on resolution, so a monitor of 1920 by 1080 pixels shows finer detail than one of 1280 by 720 pixels of the same size. Screen size in inches is a different measure: it is the diagonal length of the display.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks what the letters stand for
variantes.contenu_markdown: CRT is Cathode Ray Tube, LCD is Liquid Crystal Display, and dpi is dots per inch. Learn the full forms exactly: the mark is lost if one word is wrong.

sections.enonce_markdown: A computer centre in Buea has three jobs. (a) Print 200 copies of a question paper as fast and cheaply as possible. (b) Print a form that has three carbon layers, so that all layers are filled in at the same time. (c) Show a lesson to 40 students sitting in a hall. Choose one output device for each job, give a reason, and say whether each output is softcopy or hardcopy.

etapes.justification: A large number of pages needs speed and low cost per page.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A **laser printer** prints quickly and sharply, and its output is **hardcopy**.

etapes.justification: Several layers must be marked in one pass, which needs force at the print head.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A **dot matrix printer**: its pins strike through the layers; its output is **hardcopy**.

etapes.justification: A large group must see the same image, so the screen image has to be enlarged.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A **projector** shows the lesson on a wall or screen; its output is **softcopy**.

etapes.justification: Anything printed on paper is hardcopy and anything displayed or played is softcopy.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Laser printer for job (a), dot matrix printer for job (b) and projector for job (c). The first two give permanent hardcopy; the projector gives temporary softcopy.

items.erreur_markdown: A monitor produces hardcopy because we can see the result.
items.pourquoi_faux: Hardcopy needs a physical, lasting form such as paper. A screen image disappears when the display changes.
items.correction_markdown: A monitor gives **softcopy**; a printer gives **hardcopy**.

items.erreur_markdown: The sharpness of a screen is measured in inches.
items.pourquoi_faux: Inches give the screen size (the diagonal). Sharpness is the number of pixels.
items.correction_markdown: Sharpness is **resolution**, for example 1280 by 720 pixels; size is the diagonal in inches.

items.erreur_markdown: A scanner is an output device because it makes a copy of a page.
items.pourquoi_faux: A scanner reads a page and sends the image into the computer, so it is an input device.
items.correction_markdown: A scanner is an **input** device; a printer is the **output** device that makes the copy.

items.pourquoi_faux: The first word is wrong. The letters stand for a liquid that controls light, not for light.

items.erreur_markdown: A dot matrix printer is the best choice for coloured photographs.
items.pourquoi_faux: Its pins give coarse dots and low quality. Inkjet printers suit photographs.
items.correction_markdown: Use dot matrix for multi-part forms; use **inkjet** for coloured pictures.

items.enonce_markdown: State two differences between softcopy and hardcopy and give one example of each.
items.solution_markdown:
- Softcopy is shown on a screen or played on speakers, while hardcopy is printed on paper.
- Softcopy is temporary and easy to change, while hardcopy is permanent.

Example of softcopy: a picture on a monitor. Example of hardcopy: a page from a printer.

items.enonce_markdown: A monitor has a resolution of 1280 columns by 720 rows and a second monitor of the same size has 1920 columns by 1080 rows. Calculate the number of pixels on each screen and say which gives the sharper picture.
items.solution_markdown:
Total pixels = columns $\times$ rows.

First monitor: $1280 \times 720 = 921,600$ pixels.

Second monitor: $1920 \times 1080 = 2,073,600$ pixels.

The second monitor has 2.25 times as many pixels, so it gives the **sharper picture**.

items.enonce_markdown: A school office must print 240 pages. Printer A (laser) prints 20 pages per minute and costs 15 FCFA per page for toner and paper. Printer B (inkjet) prints 5 pages per minute and costs 25 FCFA per page for ink and paper. Calculate the time and the cost for each printer, then say which one you recommend and why.
items.solution_markdown:
Printer A: time = $240 \div 20 = 12$ minutes; cost = $240 \times 15 = 3,600$ FCFA.

Printer B: time = $240 \div 5 = 48$ minutes; cost = $240 \times 25 = 6,000$ FCFA.

Printer A saves 36 minutes and 2,400 FCFA, so I recommend **Printer A (laser)** for a large job: it is faster and cheaper per page.

items_markdown: Output devices turn processed data into information people can see or hear; softcopy is temporary, hardcopy is permanent.
Monitors, projectors and speakers give softcopy; printers and plotters give hardcopy.
CRT is Cathode Ray Tube and LCD is Liquid Crystal Display; LCD screens are flat, light and save power.
Screen sharpness is resolution in pixels (columns times rows); screen size is the diagonal in inches; printer sharpness is in dpi.
Dot matrix: pins, noisy, multi-part forms. Inkjet: ink drops, good colour. Laser: toner, fast and sharp.
